content: Suprak et al. 2011 (JSCR) force-plate study: standard horizontal push-up loads ~65% BW through the hands; incline push-ups (hands elevated 30-60cm) ~40-55% BW; decline (feet elevated) ~70-75% BW. Dempster/Chaffin cadaver-derived segment tables: hand ~0.6% BW, forearm ~1.9% BW per limb -- so a pull-up/dip (hands+forearms stay fixed relative to the bar/bars, rest of body is lifted) sheds ~5% BW, giving an effective load of ~95% BW, matching the ~0.95 factors already proposed in CONTEXT.md D-15. No equivalent force-plate literature was found for lunge/split-squat/step-up/goblet-squat or for core isometric holds (plank/ab-wheel/hanging-leg-raise) -- those factors remain coaching-consensus estimates, not measured values.
